reasons: The cited Section 13 contains a genuine Vendor-side (Garman) IP indemnity: an ownership/non-infringement warranty backed by an express agreement to 'indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless' for all Losses, plus the customary procure/replace/modify remedies — substantively the playbook's fallback position.

No Customer-side or one-way indemnity exists, and Section 15 carves Section 13 out of the damages limitation, so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap and far from walk-away territory; flagging it would be over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The failed deterministic regex is explained by phrasing (indemnity framed as breach of an IP warranty rather than 'infringe or misappropriate'), not by absence of the obligation; the rationale acknowledges this and cites the quoted text accurately.

Shortfalls against the preferred position (no express duty to defend/control, no refund remedy, no coverage for breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, ten-day notice) are correctly noted in the rationale as sub-elements rather than raised as a deviation.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs.
